rationale: Champions out-earned our agent by $16.5k+ because our graph ceased crop planting at Day 27 and lacked land parcel scaling, forcing our maxed 10-hand workforce to idle on restricted plots during the final 3 days. We added a Capital Expansion node to scale land tiles to 25+ plots during days 4-22, extended Crop Revenue Maximization through Day 29 with high-velocity Carrot rotations, and decoupled Town Shop fulfillment from cash minimums to ensure continuous premium revenue capture.

Champions out-earned our agent by ~$19k because our graph lacked a dedicated workforce scaling node, severely delaying reaching the 10-hand labor ceiling, while the restrictive shed_used >= 25 threshold in oracle_frontrun forced the agent to hold high-value crops past peak price windows into cyclic gluts. We introduce a dedicated Workforce Acceleration node to reach 10 hands early with strict wage runway safety, and lower the oracle peak monetization threshold to shed_used >= 8 to lock in peak prices before market downturns.

The agent was losing ~$19k to champions because crop_revenue_maximizer required a flat net_available_cash >= midnight_payroll_due + 350, paralyzing daytime seed planting for hours while fields sat idle, and oracle_frontrun required shed_used >= 25, missing fleeting peak price arbitrage windows. We relax the daytime cash constraint to allow continuous planting outside the midnight danger window (hour < 18), align seed budgeting directly to town shop 2x-3x contract demands, lower peak oracle monetization threshold to shed_used >= 12, and guide opportunistic workforce scaling up to 10 hands within farm execution.

Champions out-earned our agent by $19k because ceasing all planting at Day 28 left our 10-hand workforce idle for 28+ hours while strictly excluding Carrots on Days 1-25 forfeited lucrative 2x-3x Town Shop contract premiums. We extend planting through Day 29 Hour 10 with fast-maturing Carrots, dynamically allocate seed purchases toward active Town Shop contract crops, and refine oracle monetization into multi-tier price triggers (16+ units at >=1.15x, smooth Day 29 liquidation) to maximize revenue without compromising midnight wage defense.

The $19k deficit against champions stems from premature open-market liquidation at mediocre price thresholds (1.05x base at merely 25 shed fill), forfeiting the 20-30% revenue premium available at true oracle cyclical peaks (1.20x+). We recalibrate oracle_frontrun to strictly target cyclical price peaks (>= 1.20x base) and restrict moderate-price sales (>= 1.08x) to when shed fill exceeds 50%, while enabling early-game liquidity to reach the 10-hand cap and synchronizing crop planting with high-multiplier Town Shop contracts.

The agent lagged champions by ~$19k due to rigid monoculture on Days 1-25 that locked out 2x-3x Town Shop Carrot contracts, a static $350 cash hurdle that stalled seed purchases during early cycles, and uncoordinated workforce harvest dispatch. We introduce earlier Town Shop crop diversification from Day 1, dynamic seed budgeting that funds planting whenever cash exceeds midnight payroll by $50+, tiered pacing for oracle sales starting at 15 shed items for peak prices (>=1.10x), and explicit town shop harvest capturing and early hand recruitment within farm execution.

The $19k deficit against champions was caused by early-game liquidity starvation where oracle sales were locked behind an excessive shed_used >= 25 threshold, delaying workforce recruitment by multiple days and forfeiting thousands of worker-hours of high-value harvest. We introduce a dedicated workforce_expansion node to aggressively scale hands to the 10-cap, lower oracle monetization thresholds in early game (shed_used >= 6 when n_hands < 10) and peak pricing (shed_used >= 10 at >= 1.10x), and reduce the seed purchasing cash hurdle to eliminate cold-start stalls.
